name: Sidi Bouzid Beach
hero_subtitle: A popular Atlantic beach with cafés and open views.

overview.title: One of the region's favourite beaches
overview.p1: Sidi Bouzid is one of the most frequented beaches around El Jadida. It offers a long stretch of sand, beach restaurants and a lively atmosphere at weekends.
overview.p2: Ideal for swimming and a seafood lunch facing the waves. Less monumental than the citadel, more about simple seaside pleasure.
overview.p3: Reachable by grand taxi from the city centre. Often combined with a morning visit to the Portuguese City.

food.title: Eating near Sidi Bouzid
food.p1: Restaurants are mainly around the port and the corniche.
food.li1: Fish restaurants at the port (5–10 min walk).
food.li3: Simple tables in the citadel streets.
food.p2: Cash remains useful for small local places.
food.li4: Avoid eating inside heritage sites (no facilities).
food.li5: Bring water before or after the visit.

q1.question: How much time for Sidi Bouzid?
q1.answer: 30 to 60 minutes is usually enough for a good visit.

q2.question: Is there an entry fee?
q2.answer: Many outdoor areas are free; the cistern has a ticket. Check on site.

q3.question: Can I visit with children?
q3.answer: Yes, most sites are suitable for families with basic supervision.

q4.question: Is it open every day?
q4.answer: Outdoor sites are generally accessible daily; indoor sites may close one day a week.

q5.question: Do I need a guide?
q5.answer: Not required, but a local guide enriches the history of the Portuguese City.
